solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Criticises business degree in final semester primarily

indicators.note: the degree sits inside the word for final, splitting it in two
primarily points to the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: final means last
Master of Business Administration
first letter of semester

explanation.surface: A student slates the business degree they are finishing, in their very last semester.
explanation.definitionFit: To lambast someone is to criticise them harshly, so the verbs are synonyms in the same inflection.

clue.text: Spots food in dining room — no starter provided

indicators.note: with no starter, the word for a dining room loses its first letter
the food sits inside what is left of the dining room

blocks.note: a mess is a military dining room
a pie is a type of food

explanation.surface: Someone notices that the canteen has not provided any first course.
explanation.walkthrough: A mess is the dining hall of a military unit, so the food word sits in a shortened mess.
explanation.definitionFit: Espies means catches sight of, the verb sense of spots rather than the noun for blemishes.

clue.text: Shout outside with actor

indicators.note: the shout goes around the outside of the next word, enclosing it

blocks.note: to holler is to shout
and means together with

explanation.surface: Someone yells at a performer, or shouts alongside a performer on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Actor' reads as the second half of a phrase about shouting but is the definition; 'with' is the joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Hollander is an English stage and screen performer, so the name is an example of the category.

clue.text: Cold periods in prisons

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
ages are periods of time

explanation.surface: Long, chilly stretches spent behind bars.
explanation.definitionFit: Cages are enclosures that confine captives, so they serve as prisons in a looser sense.

clue.text: Dessert, one with butter, is in belly that needs reduction

indicators.note: the belly word is reduced, losing its last letter
the earlier words go inside the shortened belly

blocks.note: Roman numeral one
a ram is an animal that butts
taken as written
tum is informal for stomach

explanation.surface: A rich buttery pudding sits in a stomach that should be slimmed down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butter' looks like the dairy spread but means an animal that butts, the crossword way of naming a male sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiramisu is an Italian layered pudding of coffee-soaked sponge and mascarpone, an example of a sweet course.

clue.text: Politician in rule excluding British sailors?

indicators.note: excluding means leaving out the letters that follow from the word for rule

blocks.note: to govern is to rule
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A minister in government who keeps the navy out of things.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Gove is a British Conservative politician and former cabinet minister, an example of the category.

clue.text: Critic back around New York, heading north

indicators.note: the back word wraps around the state abbreviation
in a down clue going north means reading upwards, from bottom to top

blocks.note: the rear is the back
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A reviewer returns to New York and then travels north.
explanation.definitionFit: Jay Rayner is a well-known British restaurant reviewer, so he is an example of a critic.

clue.text: Noble perhaps to strangle old Italian poet

indicators.note: strangling grips something tightly all round, so one word holds the other

blocks.note: an aristo is an aristocrat, a noble being one example
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An aristocrat sets about throttling an elderly Italian versifier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' belongs to the wordplay, though it reads as describing the poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludovico Ariosto wrote the Renaissance epic Orlando Furioso, an example of a poet from Italy.

clue.text: Dining out with worker up in arms

indicators.note: out suggests being put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
an ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: An employee is furious about having to eat out.
explanation.definitionFit: Up in arms is an idiom for protesting angrily, matching indignant as an adjective of outrage.

clue.text: Song about endless division in state

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is cut off the next word
the song goes about, or around, the shortened division

blocks.note: an aria is a solo song in opera
a zone is a division of an area

explanation.surface: A tune concerning never-ending splits within a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Arizona is one of the fifty United States, an example of a state in the political sense.

clue.text: Journal something to fuel the fire?

blocks.note: first meaning: a written record, as kept on a ship
second meaning: a piece of wood for burning

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the second definition is a description of one use rather than a dictionary sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a daily record such as a ship's diary and a chunk of tree trunk burnt in a grate.

clue.text: Villain pounds comedian

blocks.note: a baddie is a villain
L is the symbol for pounds sterling, from libra

explanation.surface: A bad guy beats up a stand-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pounds' looks like a verb of hitting but is the money abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: David Baddiel is a British stand-up and television performer, an example of a comic.

clue.text: Finding energy in a can, dined at home

indicators.note: the energy symbol is placed inside the following words

blocks.note: a tin is a can
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone discovers an energy drink and has supper at home.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat in is to have a meal at home rather than going out, so the past tense matches dined.

clue.text: Rich Tea provided in westbound service area

indicators.note: travelling west in an across clue means reading right to left

blocks.note: Mass is a church service
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A biscuit and a cuppa are on offer at a motorway service station heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: Rich Tea is a plain British biscuit, but here it describes a strong-flavoured tea. The motorway services are a false picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Assam is a full-bodied black tea from north-east India, known for its rich malty flavour.

clue.text: Nominally commits oneself to work?

blocks.note: surface reading: someone dedicates themselves in name only
setter's reading: a person writes their name to record arrival at the workplace

explanation.walkthrough: Nominally suggests in name only, half-heartedly; read literally it means by name, by putting a signature in a register.
explanation.definitionFit: Registering arrival at a workplace by writing one's name in a book is the phrasal verb asked for.

clue.text: Bury Football Club seen in Milan

blocks.note: first meaning: to put a body in a grave
second meaning: the short name of Internazionale, a Milanese soccer team

explanation.walkthrough: Bury is also a town in Lancashire with a football club, which makes the surface read as one team visiting Milan.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to place a corpse in the ground, and Inter is the familiar name of FC Internazionale Milano.

clue.text: Halt rot in corrupt sporting event

indicators.note: corrupt means spoilt or altered, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A call to stop the rot of corruption in a sports competition.
explanation.definitionFit: A triathlon is an endurance race combining swimming, cycling and running, an example of a sports contest.

clue.text: Very pleased — glowing in fact

indicators.note: the glowing word goes inside the word for fact

blocks.note: in deed, as in 'in fact', indeed
light as an adjective means bright, glowing

explanation.surface: Someone is truly thrilled and positively beaming.
explanation.walkthrough: A deed is a legal document, an established fact; the light word splits it after DE.
explanation.definitionFit: Delighted is an adjective of great happiness, exactly the strength of very pleased.

clue.text: In which no axe cut yet if so ordered?

definitions.text: In which no axe cut yet if so ordered?

indicators.note: ordered means put into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.clueFragment: no axe cut yet if so
blocks.note: the fifteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A situation where the headsman has not swung yet, because someone in authority commanded a delay.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: when a court grants this, the axe has not yet fallen.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay of execution is a court order postponing a sentence, here pictured as a beheading held back.

clue.text: Wonderful news about alumnus who was poorly hidden?

blocks.note: OB is an old boy, a former pupil
the good news about someone who was ill is that he's (he is) cured, with 's for is

explanation.surface: Great tidings about a former student who had been unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: The wonderful news is 'OB's cured': the old boy is better. 'Poorly' is British for unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscured means concealed from view, a past participle matching hidden.

clue.text: Henry in Collins worked with author

indicators.note: the letter for Henry is placed inside the surname
worked means kneaded or shaped, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A man named Henry, employed at the publisher Collins, collaborated with a novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry looks like a first name but is the physics unit symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: David Nicholls is the English novelist who wrote One Day, an example of a writer.

clue.text: Tons eaten by female deer and fawns?

indicators.note: something eaten is taken inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a doe is a female deer
T is the abbreviation for tons

explanation.surface: Hinds and their young munch through huge quantities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fawns' looks like a noun for young deer, fitting the surface, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To fawn on someone is to show excessive affection, and dotes describes the same doting fondness.

clue.text: Journalist in act, incredibly cute

indicators.note: incredibly suggests something beyond belief, so the letters are wildly altered

blocks.note: to do is to act
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A reporter caught looking adorable in the middle of a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyse Doucet is the BBC's chief international correspondent, an example of a news reporter.

clue.text: I had one of the ears of an ass

blocks.note: I'd is short for I had
Roman numeral one
otic is the medical adjective relating to the ear

explanation.surface: A boast of owning one of a donkey's long ears.
explanation.walkthrough: The donkey picture hides that 'ass' means a fool, so 'of an ass' is a description of foolishness.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiotic means like a fool, and an ass is a stupid person, so the phrase works as an adjective.

clue.text: Popular exploit for sure

blocks.note: in means fashionable, popular
an exploit is a heroic deed

explanation.surface: A well-liked feat, without a doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: Indeed is an adverb of emphasis or confirmation, like certainly, the sense of for sure.

clue.text: Former politician, Conservative member, initially Green

indicators.note: initially signals taking the opening letter of the word after it

blocks.note: C abbreviates Conservative
a limb is a member of the body
first letter of Green

explanation.surface: An ex-MP who was a Tory party member and an environmentalist to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: The party labels mislead: Nick Clegg led the Liberal Democrats, and 'member' is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Nick Clegg was the UK's Deputy Prime Minister from 2010 to 2015, an example of an ex-statesman.

clue.text: Returned books are an inspiration

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the following letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books
taken as written

explanation.surface: Library books that come back are a source of creative ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Greek Muse of love poetry, and a Muse is the classic source of creative spirit.

clue.text: University student and no- good teacher in sacred site

indicators.note: no good means the letter for good is dropped from the following word

blocks.note: U abbreviates university
L is a learner
a guru is a spiritual teacher

explanation.surface: A college pupil and a useless tutor visit a holy place.
explanation.definitionFit: Uluru, the great red rock in central Australia, is a holy place for its Aboriginal owners, the Anangu.

clue.text: Addict taken in because relapsed

indicators.note: taken in means held inside, so the letters lie within the following words

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A drug addict is admitted to hospital after slipping back into the habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relapsed' looks like a reversal signal, but the letters read forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is informal for a drug taker, so it names an addict.

clue.text: Happy to return ring on greeting Quixote?

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the word for happy is read backwards

blocks.note: hi is a greeting
glad means happy
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Pleased to give back a ring after saying hello to Don Quixote.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: Cervantes' knight was a minor Spanish noble.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidalgo is a member of Spain's lower nobility, and Don Quixote is the most famous one in literature.

clue.text: Friar Tuck embodies cunning

indicators.note: to embody is to contain in one's body, so the letters are held within the name

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: Robin Hood's portly friar is the very picture of craftiness.
explanation.walkthrough: Friar Tuck is the jolly monk of the Robin Hood legends.
explanation.definitionFit: Art can mean craft or guile, as in artful, a less common sense matching cunning as a noun.

clue.text: Huge mountain woman tempted others

blocks.note: in Genesis, Eve tempted Adam with the apple
the rest means the others

explanation.surface: An enormous peak lured a woman, then lured other climbers too.
explanation.definitionFit: Everest, on the Nepal–Tibet border, is the highest peak on Earth, so it is the ultimate example.

clue.text: Deathless seabird entering wild lea

indicators.note: entering means going into, so the bird goes inside the other letters
wild means out of control, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: An immortal gull lands in an untamed meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: A lea is a meadow, but here it is just three letters to scramble.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternal means lasting forever, and deathless means never dying, so both say without end.
